report_title: ECDAT Enterprise Post-Quantum Cryptographic Risk Report
executive_summary: The enterprise cryptographic portfolio analyzed across 10 assets reveals significant vulnerability to quantum threats, driven by the presence of classical asymmetric algorithms such as RSA-2048, RSA-3072, RSA-4096, ECDSA, Ed25519, and deprecated primitives like 3'DES-CBC. Across the portfolio, 6 assets are classified in the HIGH risk tier [ML Risk Model], 8 assets are exposed to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) risks [HNDL Engine], and 5 assets exhibit active migration timeline deficits under Mosca's Inequality [Mosca Theorem]. With an earliest migration start deadline established at 2029.8, immediate migration planning toward NIST standards such as ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) is required.
key_findings: 6 assets (DISC-001, DISC-002, DISC-004, DISC-006, DISC-007, DISC-008) are classified as HIGH risk [ML Risk Model], driven heavily by quantum vulnerability and cryptographic role features with CatBoost confidence scores ranging between 81.5% and 87.3%.

8 assets are exposed to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later threats [HNDL Engine], with long-lived data extending up to year 2034, while 5 assets violate Mosca's Inequality (X + Y > Z) [Mosca Theorem] with migration deficits ranging from +1.2y to +4.2y.

The portfolio's earliest migration start deadline is established at 2029.8 [Mosca Theorem], requiring prioritized remediation for classical asymmetric assets (RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519) while maintaining resilient posture on native PQC (ML-KEM-768) and hybrid assets.
